en: Points of Controversy The Great Chapter The Thirteenth Sub-Chapter
The Discussion on One Bound for the Immediate:
Is it possible that a person bound for the immediate might enter the fixed course of rightness?
Yes, it is.
"Could one enter both the fixed course of wrongness and the fixed course of rightness?
"One should not say so. ...pe...
"Could a person who has been engaged for an immediate rebirth enter the fixed course of rightness?"
“Yes.
“But surely that action was engaged in, remorse was produced, and regret was generated?
“Yes.”
If that action has been undertaken, remorse produced, and regret generated, then surely it should not be said:
"A person who has undertaken [the training] immediately can enter the fixed course of rightness.
Is it not the case that a person who has undertaken [the training] immediately is incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness?

“Yes,” you say. “Has a mother been deprived of life? … Has a father been deprived of life? … Has an Arhat been deprived of life? … Has blood been shed against a Tathāgata with a malicious mind? … Has the Saṅgha been split?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … No, indeed.
Is a person who has committed an immediate offense incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness after withdrawing that action, dispelling the remorse, and removing the regret?
Yes. [The same applies if] a mother has been deprived of life... a father has been deprived of life... [and so on].
"The Saṅgha is split"?

One should not say this… [as before] … Is a person who has been engaged in that action immediately after it occurred— having withdrawn that action, having dispelled remorse, and having removed regret— incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness?
“Yes.
“But has that karma been withdrawn, remorse dispelled, and regret removed?
“Yes.”
If that action has been withdrawn, remorse dispelled, and regret removed, then surely it should not be said:
"A person who has failed in immediate application, having withdrawn that action, dispelled that remorse, and removed that regret, is incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness.
Would such a person not enter the fixed course of rightness?
“Yes.
“Was that karma not associated with him?
“Yes.”
If that action was performed by one who was engaged [in the path], then indeed it should not be said:
"A person who is not immediately engaged may enter the fixed course of rightness.
The Discussion on One Not Immediately Engaged is finished.
